tool.name: drs-transcript-prediction
tool.description: Predicts transcripts from direct RNA sequencing reads for organisms without splicing
tool.command: drs-transcript-prediction -r '$reads_bed' -d '$ranges_bed' ## An unset optional value renders as an empty string or as the string "None", ## depending on the Galaxy version; guard against both representations. #if str($chromosome).strip() not in ("", "None") -c '$chromosome' #end if --min_depth '${sec_region.min_depth}' #if str($sec_region.max_depth).strip() not in ("", "None") --max_depth '${sec_region.max_depth}' #end if --min_region_positional_depth '${sec_region.min_region_positional_depth}' --candidate_offset_len '${sec_candidate.candidate_offset_len}' --depth_delta_threshold '${sec_candidate.depth_delta_threshold}' --candidate_read_threshold '${sec_candidate.candidate_read_threshold}' --assigned_read_ratio_threshold '${sec_candidate.assigned_read_ratio_threshold}' ${candidates_only} ${verbose} ## The output prefix is fixed so the output names cannot collide with the input paths -o 'output'

param.label: Reads BED file
param.help: Position-sorted BED file of direct RNA sequencing reads. The first 6 BED columns (chrom, start, end, name, score, strand) are required. A read is only used if it lies entirely within a range of the same strand. Leading '#', 'track', 'browser' and blank lines are skipped.

param.label: Ranges BED file
param.help: BED file of distinct, non-overlapping interval ranges per strand. The first 4 columns (chrom, start, end, strand) are read and any additional columns are ignored. Leading '#', 'track', 'browser' and blank lines are skipped. A typical source is a strand-aware 'bedtools merge' over the reads BED.

param.label: Chromosome to analyze
param.help: Restrict the analysis to this single chromosome/contig ID. Leave empty to loop over all chromosomes present in the ranges file. The ID is compared as a string, so numeric chromosome names (e.g. '1') work as expected.

validator.message: Chromosome/contig IDs may only contain letters, numbers and the characters '_', '.', '-', '|', ':' and '*'.

param.label: Minimum depth per region
param.help: Minimum required depth for a distinct region to have candidate transcripts searched for.

param.label: Maximum depth per region
param.help: Maximum allowed depth for a distinct region. Regions above this depth are skipped and reported in the tool output. Leave empty to disable the maximum threshold.

param.label: Minimum positional depth within a region
param.help: Minimum required positional depth within a region. Reads mapping to positions below this threshold are discarded and new distinct sub-regions are created from the remaining runs of positions. Sub-region names gain a '/N' suffix.

param.label: Minimum distance between candidate coordinates
param.help: Candidate start/end coordinates can be very close together. When a candidate start or end coordinate is encountered, require the next candidate position to be at least this many bases away.

param.label: Depth change threshold for start/stop sites
param.help: If the absolute change in depth between two consecutive positions exceeds this number, consider it a potential transcript start or stop site.

param.label: Minimum overlapping reads per candidate
param.help: Discard a candidate transcript if the number of reads overlapping within it is below this threshold.

param.label: Minimum assigned read ratio
param.help: Ratio of reads assigned solely to a candidate transcript to all reads overlapping within that transcript. Transcripts exceeding this ratio are kept in the predicted output.

param.name: candidates_only
param.label: Output candidate transcripts only
param.help: Skip the alternative-transcript filtering step and only report the candidate transcripts BED. The predicted transcripts BED and GFF3 outputs are not produced.

param.name: verbose
param.label: Verbose output
param.help: Print the resolved arguments and per-region progress to the tool output.

tool.help:
**What it does**
**drs-transcript-prediction** (TP, "Transcript Prediction") predicts transcripts from direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) reads, such as those produced by nanopore direct RNA protocols. Because such reads start and stop at the real 5' and 3' ends of a transcript, transcript boundaries show up as sharp changes in read depth. TP:
1. Builds a per-position read depth profile for each distinct genomic range you supply. 2. Flags positions where the absolute depth change exceeds a threshold as candidate transcript **start** (depth increases) or **stop** (depth decreases) sites. 3. Combines candidate starts with candidate ends to enumerate possible transcripts. 4. Assigns reads to candidates and discards alternative transcripts that are not supported by enough reads uniquely assigned to them, resolving start/stop combinations that could otherwise explain the same reads.
**Inputs**
- **Reads BED file** — a position-sorted BED of reads. The first 6 BED columns (chrom, start, end, name, score, strand) are required. A read is only used if it lies *entirely* within one range and on the same strand. - **Ranges BED file** — distinct, non-overlapping interval ranges, one line per range and strand. The first 4 columns (chrom, start, end, strand) are read and extra columns are ignored. A convenient way to build this is to merge your reads per strand, e.g. `bedtools merge -i reads.bed -s -c 6,4 -o distinct,count`, keeping the ranges with enough support. - **Chromosome to analyze** — optionally restrict the run to a single chromosome/contig ID.
**Outputs**
- **Candidate transcripts (BED)** — every candidate transcript considered, before filtering. BED6: chrom, start, end, name, score (`.`), strand. Names are `R_<region>_T<n>`; a region name of the form `R_<region>/<split>` indicates a sub-region created by the minimum positional depth filter. - **Predicted transcripts (BED)** — the candidates that pass the read-count and read-assignment ratio cutoffs. - **Predicted transcripts (GFF3)** — the same transcripts as GFF3 (source `tp.py`, type `transcript`, `ID=<name>`), with a normalized prediction score in the score column. Coordinates are converted to 1-based/inclusive, so they are offset by one base from the BED output.
The predicted transcripts BED and GFF3 are not produced when *Output candidate transcripts only* is enabled.
**Tuning the prediction**
- *Minimum/Maximum depth per region* — regions whose depth is below the minimum or above the maximum are skipped entirely; skipped regions are listed in the tool output. - *Minimum positional depth within a region* — positions with less support are dropped and the remaining contiguous runs of positions become new sub-regions. Useful to split ranges that were merged too aggressively. - *Minimum distance between candidate coordinates* — collapses candidate starts/ends that are nearly identical; lower it to resolve closely spaced isoform boundaries. - *Depth change threshold* — the core sensitivity knob. Lower values call more (and weaker) start/stop sites, producing more candidates. - *Minimum overlapping reads per candidate* — drops candidates with too little read support. - *Minimum assigned read ratio* — how much of a candidate's read support must be uniquely assignable to it. Raise it to keep only confidently distinguished isoforms.
-----
**References**
- Mattick JSA, Bromley RE, Watson KJ, Adkins RS, Holt CI, Lebov JF, Sparklin BC, Tyson TS, Rasko DA, Dunning Hotopp JC. *Deciphering transcript architectural complexity in bacteria and archaea.* mBio. 2024.
